note: A dataset-grain holdings_period is one pooled range, never per-edition claims; an undated declaration (all_versions) is not annual evidence and forms no state, even where the variant delivers two editions (2020 and 2021). Expected literals: the pool state (2002-01-01, 2020-12-31, pooled 1, data_type text) from test_holdings_period_converts_to_one_pooled_range (variable_state row == ('2002-01-01', '2020-12-31', 1); effect.fields.data_type == value_field('text')); the undated column's unsupported_occurrence and absent state from test_column_declaration_preserves_only_supplied_flags_and_periods[FIX-None] (segments == (), issues == {unsupported_occurrence}) and test_declared_pooled_edition_is_retained_without_inferred_annual_states (no inferred annual segment, unsupported_occurrence). The undated addition's evidence is one delivered record of its variant (the old test: addition.support_records == (record,), the context's only record). With two delivered rows that record is the variant's first row in source order (convert_column_entry adds `record_ref(records[0])` for an undated entry), here A's: register 1, variant 2, edition 2020 (its regver_id), variable 5, member 20 (its cvid), written in the README's ref form. Step 2 reverses the rows. The pool column raises no issue: test_holdings_period_converts_to_one_pooled_range asserts no conversion blockers and `formed.diagnostics == ()`.
fails_if: `scb_errata.convert_column_entry` expands a holdings_period into per-edition additions or drops its pooled bounds, so pool is not one pooled 2002-2020 state; or it dates an undated (all_versions) declaration with an edition's annual scope, or adds one per delivered edition, instead of one `TemporalScope(kind="unknown")` addition, so undated gets a state and no unsupported_occurrence; or it anchors the undated addition on no delivered record or on every record of the variant, so its issue cites no ref or two
